Repro PoCs hardcoded the shadow root path (mantis_shadow/unfixed, plan_fixed), so re-running them against patched shadows produced false STILL-TRIGGERS verdicts. Repro and patch checks must parameterize the target root (sys.path via argv or inline `python -c`), never embed the shadow path.

patch_ratelimit assumed every route imports from app.core.database.get_db, but contact.py imports neither get_db nor Depends, so the generated dependency silently broke the route (NameError: rate_limit/Depends undefined) and the attack check falsely reported THROTTLED. Lesson: when injecting imports, inspect each target file's actual import lines; verify patched trees by importing the app in a subprocess, and assert on positive markers ('ATTACK_429_SEEN True') rather than absence of a negative one.

Inline verification scripts formatted with % must escape literal %d as %%d; one unescaped %d inside a JSON payload crashed the whole patch run with 'TypeError: not enough arguments for format string'. Also avoid %-formatting inside scripts that contain user data with % characters.

The F3 sink check first failed (NOT-TRIGGERED) because the payload name 'T' violates the Pydantic min_length=2 constraint and 422s before reaching the route. Attack payloads must satisfy upstream validation to exercise the vulnerable path.

Starlette echoes access-control-allow-origin and -methods even when the requested header is disallowed (it simply omits the header from the allow list). Verdicts must parse each echoed CORS header separately (origin AND methods AND headers), not test substring presence of the requested method.

THREAT_MODEL marks API startup availability as CRITICAL tier; per calibrate rules that lifts the DoS cap, letting the two boot-blocking findings (plan.py self-import, contact undefined classes) land at CRITICAL 8.0. Documenting availability tiers in the threat model materially changes final risk scores.

A minimal in-memory per-IP rate limit (defaultdict of timestamps under a lock, 10/min -> HTTP 429) wired as a FastAPI dependency _rl: None = Depends(rate_limit) is an idiomatic minimal fix for CWE-287 in a small FastAPI app; verified: bursts of 12/25 see 429, 3 benign requests pass.

For route-level CWE-209 verification, monkeypatching the module-global service function (lead_mod.create_lead_service) before TestClient requests reliably drives exceptions into the route's except block, reproducing the leak without touching the DB.
